text:
ike: quick thought 1: we're losing followup momentum on PMs. propose a tiny pattern called 'triage-bump' 1: make the first 72h super explicit so owners don't drop it. sketch below.
neha: curious1: what does super explicit mean? reminders? stronger defaults?
ike: defaults + automated nudges: when PM publishes, create 3 short checkpoints: C1=T+24h (owner confirms plan), C2=T+48h (progress note), C3=T+72h (PR/infra request or blocker + escalation). if blocked at C3, auto-assign shadow and require unblock reason.
paul: like it. keep fields tiny: owner, shadow, one-line fix, SLA-tier, evidence link (for close), recurrence-tag. short and scannable.
yasmin: add a mandatory "acceptance test" line so verifier knows what to check (metric link or smoke test). prevents fuzzy closes.
ike: sample card body to paste:```
- Incident: <id>
- Owner: <name>
- Shadow: <name>
- SLA-tier: rapid|normal|extended
- One-line fix: <what we change>
- Acceptance test: <metric link or smoke>
- Evidence: <link>
- Recurrence-tag: <e.g., deploy-failure>
- Unblock reason (if slipped): <short text>
```
neha: automation ask: oncall-bot creates the card and posts a thread reminder at C1/C2/C3. make C3 escalate to shadow if no update and add a tiny log of the unblock reason to the postmortem doc.
oncall-bot: automated: created triage-bump item TB-33000 for incident 3300001234, assigned to @ike, shadow @neha. reminders scheduled at T+24h/T+48h/T+72h. link: https://tracker.example/TB-33000
paul: comms shorthand for execs: one-line incident summary, top open action + ETA, and whether it's blocked. that's it.
yasmin: recommend a monthly "stuck reasons" rollup using the unblock reason text to identify procurement or unclear ownership trends.
ike: next steps: 1) neha to prototype bot flow this week, 2) paul to add the card template to /incidents/process, 3) yasmin to sketch the acceptance-test examples. i'll run a one-week pilot on high-priority PMs.
neha: i'll start prototyping and ping owners to opt into the pilot.
ike: thanks all 1 :thumbsup: drop edits or PRs.
